hints.title: Interleaved Slot Assignment
hints.text: To prevent identical values from neighboring each other, fill alternating slots: first populate even indices 0, 2, 4, ... then populate odd indices 1, 3, 5, ...

hints.title: Most Frequent First
hints.text: Count element frequencies and sort items in descending order of frequency. Placing the most frequent item across even positions first ensures it cannot collide with itself.

hints.title: Alternating Fill Traversal
hints.text: Start an index pointer at 0. Write each value frequency times, advancing by 2 each step. Whenever the pointer reaches or exceeds n, reset it to 1 and continue.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from collections import Counter

class Solution:
    def rearrangeBarcodes(self, barcodes: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        counts = Counter(barcodes)
        sorted_items = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])
        n = len(barcodes)
        res = [0] * n
        idx = 0
        for code, freq in sorted_items:
            for _ in range(freq):
                if idx >= n:
                    idx = 1
                res[idx] = code
                idx += 2
        return res
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Arbitrary placement or backtracking risks creating adjacent duplicates and incurring exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting unique counts and filling alternating slots takes O(N) time and O(N) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that even-odd placement sorted by frequency guarantees separation.
complexity.notes: Guaranteed valid arrangement exists by problem constraints.
